chosen.premise: Rhydon’s brain developed after it stood on two legs, because standing freed its forelegs.
chosen.hook: Rhydon didn’t get smarter until it stood up.
chosen.visualIdea: Show Rhyhorn rising onto its hind legs as its forelegs unlock and a brain graphic lights up.
chosen.note: A very Rhydon-specific causal contradiction: standing freed its forelegs, and the Pokédex directly links that change to brain development and intelligence.

candidates.premise: Standing on its hind legs made Rhydon smarter—but its Pokédex profile still calls it very forgetful.
candidates.hook: Rhydon evolved a better brain… and still forgot everything.
candidates.visualIdea: Rhydon solves a rock puzzle, celebrates, then immediately forgets what it just figured out.
candidates.note: The smarter-but-forgetful contradiction is memorable and easy to dramatize. The evolution-method citation does not support the premise, but the Platinum and hind-leg entries do.

candidates.premise: Rhydon’s horn rotates like a drill and can shatter uncut diamonds and bore through bedrock.
candidates.hook: Rhydon’s horn is a rotating drill that can break diamonds.
candidates.visualIdea: Zoom into the spinning horn as it drills through bedrock, then cracks an uncut diamond.
candidates.note: The rotating horn, diamonds, and bedrock make a clean visual mechanic with strong support, though drill-based power is a fairly familiar Rhydon angle.

candidates.premise: Rhydon evolves from Rhyhorn at level 42, then needs a trade while holding a Protector to evolve again.
candidates.hook: Rhydon’s evolution path changes from leveling up to trading.
candidates.visualIdea: A two-step evolution track hits level 42, then stops until a trade and Protector are shown.
candidates.note: The evolution path is precise and useful for gameplay-focused fans, but it is more of a progression fact than a distinctive character premise.

candidates.premise: Rhydon’s rotating horn can destroy buildings, but one sweeping tail blow can topple one too.
candidates.hook: Rhydon doesn’t need its drill to destroy a building.
candidates.visualIdea: Compare two attack shots: the horn drills through a building, then the tail sweeps its base down.
candidates.note: The horn-versus-tail comparison is concrete and visually strong, though the cited entries say the horn destroys tall buildings and the tail topples a building, not necessarily that both attacks work the same way.

candidates.premise: Rhydon’s armor-like hide lets it live in 3,600°F molten lava and repel direct cannon hits.
candidates.hook: What could survive lava and a cannon blast without feeling it?
candidates.visualIdea: Split-screen: Rhydon submerged in 3,600°F lava, then a cannonball bouncing off its hide.
candidates.note: The lava temperature and cannon-proof hide are unusually extreme and highly visual, but “without feeling it” and “repel direct cannon hits” overstate what the cited entries actually say.

rounds.request: Not applicable: a strong angle is available. If developing alternatives, they would need an equally specific Rhydon-only contradiction or mechanism, with every hook claim tightly matched to the cited Pokédex wording.
